questions.question_text: How many terms of the arithmetic series $2 + 5 + 8 + 11 + \dots$ are needed to give a sum of $155$?

options.why: Miscalculated the quadratic roots from $3n^2 + n - 310 = 0$.
Subtracted $1$ from the positive root solution.
Selected the numerator of the extraneous negative root $-31/3$.

questions.question_text: Find the number of terms of the series $20 + 18 + 16 + \dots$ required to make the partial sum $S_n = 0$.

options.why: Used $20$ terms without accounting for the zero-sum midpoint.
Gave the trivial root $n = 0$ instead of the positive solution.
Added $1$ extra term beyond the zero sum.

questions.question_text: For the decreasing series $15 + 13 + 11 + \dots$, which two values of $n$ give a partial sum of $63$?

options.why: Selected integers that sum to $16$ but have a product different from $63$.
Chose symmetrical values around $8$ that do not satisfy the quadratic.
Omitted the second valid positive integer solution.

questions.question_text: How many terms of the arithmetic series $5 + 9 + 13 + \dots$ must be summed to equal $230$?

options.why: Used $a + nd$ instead of $a + (n - 1)d$ when setting up the quadratic.
Took the magnitude of the rejected fractional root $-23/2$.
Miscalculated the factorisation of $2n^2 + 3n - 230 = 0$.

questions.question_text: Find the least number of terms of the series $36 + 31 + 26 + \dots$ for which the partial sum $S_n$ is negative.

options.why: Found the last term for which the sum is still non-negative ($S_{15} \ge 0$).
Added an extra term beyond the minimal threshold.
Truncated the inequality $n > 15.4$ instead of taking the next whole integer.

questions.question_text:
An arithmetic series has $d = 2$, last term $l = 25$, and sum $S_n = 168$.
If the first term is $a = 3$, find the number of terms $n$.

options.why: Selected the alternative root $n = 14$ which corresponds to $a = -1$.
Averaged the two roots $12$ and $14$.
Subtracted $1$ from the correct root.

questions.question_text: How many terms of the arithmetic series $-5 - 2 + 1 + 4 + \dots$ are needed to obtain a sum of $203$?

options.why: Took the numerator of the rejected negative root $-\dfrac{29}{3}$.
Subtracted $1$ from the quadratic root.
Added $1$ extra term to the quadratic root.

questions.question_text:
The sum of $n$ terms of an AP is $S_n = n(35 - n)$.
Which two values of $n$ give a sum of $300$?

options.why: Selected numbers summing to $35$ with product $250$ instead of $300$.
Miscalculated factor pairs of $300$.
Omitted the second positive integer root.
